How is selling a house organized in Texas?

Selling in Texas runs through the county, because the county is where valuation, tax billing and deed filing happen. Texas has 254 counties, more than any other state. Harris County is the most populous, with 5,045,026 residents. Brewster County is the largest by area at 6,192 square miles, and Rockwall County is the smallest at 149 square miles.

That spread matters for a seller. A house in Rockwall and a house in Harris can sit in the same state and still deal with different appraisal districts, different tax offices and different clerks.

For a quick sense of who handles what, use this table.

TaskWho handles it
Valuing your property each yearCounty appraisal district (values are set as of Jan. 1)
Setting tax ratesEach city, county, school district and special district
Collecting the tax billOften the county tax assessor-collector, with bills out around Oct. 1
Recording deeds and other instrumentsCounty clerk, who serves as county recorder
Protesting a valueAppraisal review board, after you file with the district

How do Texas property taxes work when you sell?

Texas has no state property tax. The Comptroller says local governments set the rates and keep the money, and the state receives nothing from them. A single house can be taxed by a city, a county, a school district and special districts at the same time.

The appraisal district appraises your house as of January 1. Taxes for the year are generally due by January 31 of the following year, and penalties and interest typically start February 1 on unpaid bills. If you sell in the middle of a year, the title company usually handles the split on the settlement statement, so ask for an itemized copy early. Our Texas property tax guide covers the penalty schedule, and the city and county guides link to local offices.

Two dates are worth putting on a calendar:

  • The Comptroller's calendar lists the last day to file most protests with the appraisal review board as May 15, or the 30th day after the notice is delivered, whichever is later.
  • Tax bills are mailed around October 1, and last year's taxes become delinquent on February 1.

If you think the value is too high, our property tax protest guide walks through the hearing. If the bill is already behind, see Texas tax deed sales for what a taxing unit can do next.

What does the Texas homestead exemption mean for a seller?

The Texas residence homestead exemption lowers the value used for school district tax. The Comptroller lists a $140,000 exemption for school districts, plus an additional $60,000 for homeowners who are 65 or older or disabled. You apply on Form 50-114 with the appraisal district in the county where the house sits.

The Comptroller page says the general deadline is before May 1. Because deadlines for some exemptions differ, confirm yours with your local appraisal district. More detail is in our homestead exemption guide.

How does foreclosure work in Texas, and how fast is it?

Texas foreclosure under a deed of trust moves by notice and public auction, and the clock is short. Under Property Code Section 51.002, the sale is a public auction held between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. on the first Tuesday of a month. If the first Tuesday falls on January 1 or July 4, the sale moves to the first Wednesday.

  • On a residence, the mortgage servicer must give the borrower at least 20 days to cure the default before notice of sale can be given.
  • Notice of sale must go out at least 21 days before the sale date.
  • The notice is posted at the courthouse door, filed with the county clerk and mailed by certified mail to each obligated debtor.

Put those together and a borrower who gets a default letter can face an auction in roughly six weeks, so the first Tuesday on the notice is the date to plan around. A sale that closes before the auction can pay the loan from the proceeds, with any equity going to you. Read the Texas foreclosure process and deed of trust guides for the options before the sale.

How do you sell an inherited house in Texas?

A will does not prove title by itself in Texas. Under Estates Code Section 256.003, a will may not be admitted to probate after the fourth anniversary of the testator's death unless the applicant shows they were not in default in failing to present it by then. The probate process guide explains the steps.

When there is no will and the estate is small, there is a shorter route. Estates Code Section 205.001 lets distributees of an intestate decedent take the estate without a personal representative if these conditions are met:

  • At least 30 days have passed since the death.
  • No petition for a personal representative is pending or has been granted.
  • The estate is worth no more than $75,000, not counting homestead and exempt property.
  • An affidavit is filed with the court clerk and the judge approves it.

Estates differ, and a house can push an estate well past those limits, so talk to a Texas probate attorney before you list. We also have guides on the small estate affidavit and the affidavit of heirship.

What must a Texas seller disclose?

A seller of residential property with no more than one dwelling unit generally gives the buyer a written seller's disclosure notice under Property Code Section 5.008. It asks about the roof, items not in working order, known defects in structural components and more. Flood is a named topic. The notice asks about present flood insurance, previous flooding from a reservoir failure or breach, and previous water penetration into a structure from a natural flood event. It also asks whether the property sits wholly or partly in a 100-year floodplain, a 500-year floodplain, a floodway, a flood pool or a reservoir.

The statute lists exemptions, including transfers by a fiduciary administering a decedent's estate, foreclosure sales, and transfers to a spouse or a close relative in the direct line. If you are unsure whether your sale is covered, ask the title company or an attorney.

What do you need to know about selling a house with tenants?

Many Texas sellers own a rental. For a month-to-month tenancy, either side can end it by notice, and the notice period can be changed by a signed agreement under Property Code Section 91.001. A landlord cannot keep a tenant out of the home to show or sell it. Under Section 92.0081, the penalty is one month's rent plus $1,000, along with actual damages, court costs and attorney's fees.

For an eviction, Section 24.005 generally requires at least three days' written notice to vacate before a forcible detainer suit, unless the lease sets a different period. See our guide to selling a rented house and the eviction process page before you send anything.

Who handles closing and title in Texas?

Closings run through a title company, which searches the county records for liens, judgments and heirs, and issues the settlement statement. Texas sets title insurance premium rates by regulation. Insurance Code Section 2703.151 says the commissioner fixes the rates and bars a company from charging a different rate. In plain terms, comparing two title companies on the premium itself will not save much, so compare service and timing.

The county clerk serves as the county recorder under Local Government Code Section 191.001, so deeds filed for your property go through that office. See Texas property records and closing costs

What does an as-is cash sale look like in Texas?

In an as-is cash sale you sell the house in its current condition, so there are no repair requests and no loan approval to wait on. You still have a title search, a settlement statement and a closing through a title company. We buy directly or bring a vetted cash buyer. To start, tell us about the property and the situation, and we will tell you what we can do.

Frequently asked questions

How many counties are in Texas?

Texas has 254 counties, more than any other state.

When are Texas property taxes due?

Generally by January 31 of the year after the tax year. Penalties and interest typically start on February 1.

How long does a Texas foreclosure take?

On a residence, the servicer gives at least 20 days to cure, then the notice of sale goes out at least 21 days before an auction held on the first Tuesday of a month.

How long can a will wait to be probated in Texas?

A will generally cannot be admitted after the fourth anniversary of the death unless the applicant shows they were not in default in presenting it.

What is the small estate affidavit limit?

$75,000 in value, not counting homestead and exempt property, and only when there is no will and no personal representative has been appointed or petitioned for.

How much notice does a landlord give before eviction filing?

Generally at least three days' written notice to vacate, unless the lease sets a different period.

Can I sell a Texas house with tenants in it?

Yes, but a landlord cannot lock a tenant out to show or sell it. Read the lease and the notice rules first.

Do I need to disclose flooding when I sell?

A seller's disclosure notice asks about flood insurance, past flooding and floodplain location, with some exemptions. Ask your title company which applies.
